A.explanation: Air resistance starts at $0$ when speed is zero and rises to a constant value at terminal velocity, matching force $X$. Resultant force starts at weight and falls to $0$ when drag balances weight, matching force $Y$.

B.explanation: Weight $W = mg$ is constant during the fall and cannot fall to zero as force $Y$ does.

C.explanation: Upthrust on the ball in air is small and almost constant, so it cannot start at zero and rise as force $X$ does.

D.explanation: Neither upthrust nor weight has the shown time variation, since both are essentially constant while the ball falls.

hints: Notice the starting values: force $X$ starts at $0$ at $t=0$ when the ball is released from rest, while force $Y$ starts at its maximum and later becomes zero.
Recall that air resistance depends on speed, so it is zero at release and grows as the ball accelerates, while weight stays constant.
Write the downward resultant as weight minus air resistance and check which pair gives one rising curve levelling off and one falling curve reaching zero at terminal velocity.
walkthrough: The ball falls from rest, so initial speed $v = 0$ and final speed is constant terminal velocity with $a = 0$.
Weight acts downward and is constant. Air resistance acts upward and increases with speed, from $0$ at release to equal to weight at terminal velocity.
Therefore a force that starts at $0$ and rises to a plateau matches air resistance. This is the shape of force $X$.
The downward resultant force is $F = W - R$, where $R$ is air resistance. At $t=0$, $R=0$ so $F=W$ at its maximum. At terminal velocity, $R=W$ so $F=0$.
This falling-to-zero shape matches force $Y$. Upthrust in air is tiny and nearly constant, so it fits neither graph.
Hence force $X$ is air resistance and force $Y$ is resultant force. This is option A.
